profile.name: Zani
profile.introduction: A member of Averardo Vault's security team and holder of "Best Employee" for longer than she cares to count. She has made plenty of plans for her free time, but for now, her biggest mission is simple: clocking out on time.
profile.review:
Zani is a 5-star Spectro Gauntlets DPS who specializes in dealing high damage during the stance she enters in her Ultimate called “Inferno Mode”. Her kit is centered around certain key elements, the most important one being Spectro Frazzle which she passively and instantly converts into “Heliacal Ember” in order to charge her Ultimate Forte points, called “Blaze” which she needs in order to execute her combos to access her damage.

Key Mechanics

As said earlier, Zani’s main focus will be to build up Blaze for her to use during her Inferno Mode stance. It stacks up to 150 points, so the goal with Zani will be to reach that threshold. There are a few ways to do this:

  • Entering Inferno Mode (via her Ultimate, 50 points);

  • Using her Enhanced Skill “Crisis Response Protocol” (10 points);

  • Converting Spectro Frazzle into Heliacal Ember (5 points per stack).

Heliacal Ember works as a variant to Spectro Frazzle which stacks up to 60 times, but it does not count as Spectro Frazzle, so it does not benefit from any buffs related to it, and as a matter of fact it does not even count as a Negative Status. The only exception is they serve as a way to activate the Eternal Radiance set effects. However, the damage granted by Heliacal Ember is instantaneous and equivalent to the damage Spectro Frazzle would’ve normally dealt.

Zani has another Forte Gauge called “Redundant Energy” that allows her to cast an Enhanced Skill when fully replenished, which restores some Blaze. As Zani cannot apply any Spectro Frazzle by herself, it is important to restore some blaze, and give Zani an extra Heliacal Ember to activate Eternal Radiance Echo bonuses as well as a 20% Spectro Frazzle DMG Amplify effect for 14s to further increase her Inferno Mode damage potential, making it especially important to build before using her Ultimate. There are a few ways to do this:

  • Using her Basic Attacks;

  • Using her skill “Standard Defense Protocol” and its parry variant “Pinpoint Strike”;

  • Using her Intro Skill.

Zani’s Resonance Skill indeed allows her to first do a small hit of damage (Standard Defense Protocol) and then enter a parry stance that she can hold for up to 2 seconds, during which she takes no damage for 1 attack (and 30% reduced DMG in the 2 seconds that follow). If an attack is successfully parried, she will execute Pinpoint Strike for extra damage and Redundant Energy, which is enough to cast her Enhanced Skill after an Intro. To get all 100 Redundant Energy points without a parry, following or preceding an Intro Skill with Standard Defense Protocol into Basic Attack 3 should be all that’s needed for quick access to her Enhanced Skill. Once this is achieved, Zani is ready to activate her Ultimate and enter Inferno Mode.

During Inferno Mode, Zani gets a new kit featuring new Basic Attacks, a new parry Skill with a new counter (which also doubles as a Dodge Counter), and she utilizes her other Forte bar to execute all of these actions. She gets 50 Blaze points which she’ll consume to execute her combos in Inferno Mode (with the cap extended from 100 to 150 and her Ultimate filling those missing 50 points). All of the damage she can deal during this stance is considered Heavy Attack DMG and Spectro Frazzle DMG simultaneously, so all related buffs apply. 

Inferno Mode & How it Works

To get into the details of her Ultimate, once Zani enters Inferno Mode, she gains new Basic Attacks called “Daybreak”, “Dawning”, and “Nightfall”. These are the center of her kit in general. The simplest possible rotation only requires you to perform her Basic Attack string 2 times, which casts each of these skills twice. Simple and effective. Daybreak consumes 10 Blaze, Dawning consumes 20 Blaze and Nightfall consumes up to 40 Blaze, with each Blaze consumed giving an extra multiplier increase to Nightfall specifically (other attacks do not benefit from this). That’s 140 Blaze consumed at maximum in total.

However, other options are available. Her Skill allows you to immediately enter a parry stance for up to 2 seconds during which she will take up to 70% reduced damage. Parrying any attack triggers an equivalent to Dawning called “Lightsmash” which consumes 20 Blaze, after which Zani can immediately follow with Nightfall. This combo therefore only costs 60 Blaze. The exact same thing occurs if a Dodge Counter is executed. This can be important to factor in to preserve Blaze for lengthier rotations.

Finally, once Zani has consumed enough Blaze and has 30 left or less (the threshold is indicated on her Forte bar), then she can cast another Ultimate called “The Last Stand” which deals some damage, stops in-game timers and prevents you from switching out during it like any regular Ultimate would. This also ends her rotation as it ends Inferno Mode at the same time.

Once all of this is done, she may cast her Outro. It deals a final burst of damage dependent on the stacks of Heliacal Ember present on enemies, consumes all Heliacal Ember stacks present on targets, and also amplifies the Spectro DMG of all characters except Zani by 20% if they have Heliacal Ember applied, which is a small DMG boost for your Supports.

Meta Position & Conclusion

Zani’s position in the meta is… interesting, to say the least. Her and her teammates are fully compatible with Quickswap, and her damage can be taken to a much higher ceiling than her baseline performance. The issues arise when discussing her teammates, and her baseline performance.

Without a doubt, for a character as old as Zani, her ceiling in Quickswap is satisfactory and has withstood the test of time as she is still considered meta-viable when fully optimized. However, this performance is completely dependent on 2 very specific characters: Phoebe and Spectro Rover.

Phoebe is a necessary inclusion to her teams, no matter how you put it. Spectro Rover is not sufficient as a Frazzle applier and a buffer. Phoebe doubles Zani’s damage, simply put, and that’s not something Rover alone can compensate for. She applies more Frazzle, her buffs are so much better and tailored towards Zani specifically. Zani was simply balanced around Phoebe, a fact that makes Zani’s teambuilding restrictive, and her team options have indeed stagnated so badly that they have not changed at all since her release. Without Phoebe, Zani is quite literally worse than any Limited DPS that came out before her.

Zani, Phoebe and Spectro Rover are the prime Spectro Frazzle team, and it hasn’t changed since version 2.3, Zani’s own release date. The Frazzle application of all of these team members together is high enough that, since none of their buffs expire upon swapping, Zani can utilize her excellent Swap Cancel windows on her Nightfall attacks and preserve some Blaze in order to cast 3 or even 4 Nightfalls per full team rotation. This leads to huge DPS increases if it can be pulled off fast enough via Quickswap.

Without Quickswap, Zani and Phoebe are best used with Shorekeeper, and the performance of that team is… questionable at best. The lowest of any 2.x team, falling behind Carlotta by a noticeable margin. Not to mention, the Energy Regen requirements on that team are huge and near-impossible to meet which makes building the team very difficult, and to rub salt into the wound, that’s a full premium team, so it’s crazy expensive to pull together.

In conclusion, Zani is in one of the most unfortunate meta positions in Wuthering Waves. Only functional in a single team using Quickswap, for casual players she’ll be a struggle to get any noticeable results with, her teams are expensive to get up and running, and they take a lot of effort to pull off. Calling Zani one of the worst current investments you could make in Wuthering Waves, particularly as a new player, is a safe claim to make.
profile.pros:
• Much higher damage ceiling than her baseline performance, thanks to her very high affinity for Quickswap;

  • Looks REALLY cool in her Ultimate stance (factually speaking);

  • Has some of the most resistant shirt buttons known to mankind. I want to know who made that shirt, might be THE brand to buy from.
profile.cons:
• Without Quickswap, her damage ceiling is the lowest of any 2.x character, her teams have seen no improvements since release and are very unlikely to receive any upgrades in the future;

  • So overly reliant on Phoebe to perform it’s comical, baseline damage without Phoebe is lower than any limited 1.x DPS, Signature weapons for both her and Phoebe are also good damage increases that she nowadays needs to compete with the rest of the cast in Quickswap (even still modern teams played at a baseline level outperform the best Zani Quickswap you can do);

  • In order to truly draw out her full potential, she needs to take away Rover from more modern teams to use as a Support. Her overly restrictive teambuilding restricts other characters’ on your account, too.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to play 

Zani’s rotation goal is to get off as many Nightfall attacks as possible, as quickly as possible, while getting all of her self-buffs up and running. To do this, other teammates must apply Spectro Frazzle either before or during her Inferno Mode, and she must fill her first Forte gauge. Below are some of the ways you can do this.

Echo Timing

Summon Capitaneus at any point in her rotation.

Standard Rotation (2 Nightfall)

This is the rotation that doesn’t require any Quickswap. It’s quite weak by modern standards, but may be enough to land you clearing scores in Matrix with Phoebe by Zani’s side. In the Opener, make sure to do the Skill + Basic 3 after Zani’s Intro as well to get her Forte Skill ready.

  • Intro

  • Skill: Targeted Action

  • Ultimate: Rekindle

  • Basic: Daybreak

  • Basic: Dawning

  • Basic: Nightfall

  • Basic: Daybreak

  • Basic: Dawning

  • Basic: Nightfall (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: The Last Stand

  • Skill

  • Basic 3 (Swap)

  • Outro

3 Nightfall Rotation (S6/Quickswap)

This rotation either works at S6 or with Phoebe+Spectro Rover, by replenishing Blaze in the middle of Zani’s rotation, thanks to this team applying more Spectro Frazzle than Zani can build in advance. At S6, the following rotation requires no Quickswap, as it restores Blaze for Zani mid-rotation. Make sure to cast Skill + Basic 3 before this rotation starts in the Opener to save time. Targeted Action can also be pre-built and cast in Quickswap if you want to take this rotation to the next level.

  • Intro

  • Skill: Targeted Action (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: Rekindle

  • Basic: Daybreak

  • Basic: Dawning

  • Basic: Nightfall (Swap)

→ Replenish Spectro Frazzle here

  • Basic: Daybreak

  • Basic: Dawning

  • Basic: Nightfall (Swap)

→ If needed, replenish some more Spectro Frazzle here

  • Basic: Daybreak

  • Basic: Dawning

  • Basic: Nightfall (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: The Last Stand

  • Skill

  • Basic 3 (Swap)

  • Outro

This rotation takes an extensive amount of time, but if enough time can be saved via Quickswap, then this is always worth it to execute and quite simple compared to other Quickswap rotations in the game.

Additional Tips & Tricks

As mentioned in the 3 Nightfall rotation, Zani has many Swap Cancel windows. Her Basic 3, her Dawning and Nightfall attacks, and her Targeted Action Skill all make for great windows to save time and execute her rotation while other teammates execute their own. The more time you save, the likelier you are to gain big DPS increases from doing the 3 Nightfall rotation. In other words: more time saves, more Nightfalls, more damage. Since none of the buffs on her team are lost on swap, you can swap to your heart’s content in the middle of everybody’s rotation.

Keep in mind that a lot of this can be utilized in even the Phoebe + Scorekeeper team composition, just that you’ll only be able to squeeze in some minor Phoebe and Shorekeeper attacks to make your loop faster and deal slightly more damage. If you push this team the furthest you can, you may find the time to cast 3 Nightfalls per rotation as well, if you save a lot of time through Quickswap that you can spend holding down Zani’s Skill twice in her Ultimate rotation, or if you get lucky with parries.

Zani can even execute up to 4 Nightfalls in the Phoebe + Spectro Rover team if Phoebe saves her Ultimate to do it in the middle of Zani’s rotation and Spectro Rover cycles them quickly thanks to their slightly shorter Ultimate cooldown of 20s. However, making this worth it over 3 Nightfall requires some very advanced Quickswap that most Zani players, even Zani mains, won’t be able to pull off without it coming at a DPS loss over a full run’s worth of rotations. Ultimately, sticking to a 25s-long 3 Nightfall loop with a fast Opener rotation to cycle more Zani Ultimates over a full run is how far we recommend to optimize Zani to make her still have a viable spot in the meta.

skills.name: Routine Negotiation
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 4 consecutive attacks to deal Spectro DMG.

After performing Basic Attack Stage 3, Press Normal Attack at the right time to perform Basic Attack Breakthrough, which can be followed by Basic Attack Stage 4 by pressing Normal Attack again.

Following Basic Attack Stage 3, Basic Attack Stage 4 can also be triggered by dodging and pressing Normal Attack within a certain time after Basic Attack Stage 3.

Heavy Attack

Consume STA to attack the target, dealing Spectro DMG. Press Normal Attack within a certain time to perform Basic Attack Stage 3.

Mid-air Attack

Consume STA to perform a plunging attack, dealing Spectro DMG. Press Normal Attack within a certain time to perform Basic Attack Stage 3.

Dodge Counter

Press successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Spectro DMG. Then press Normal Attack at the right time to cast Basic Attack Breakthrough.

If Dodge Counter is not followed by Basic Attack Stage 4, press Normal Attack on the ground within a certain time to cast Basic Attack Stage 4.

skills.name: Restless Watch
skills.description:
Standard Defense Protocol

Attack the target to deal Spectro DMG and enter a block stance. This state ends early if Zani is switched off the field. Press Normal Attack within a certain time to perform Basic Attack Stage 3, recovering 10 points of Redundant Energy and Stagnating the target on hit.

When attacked by the enemy in the block stance, reduce this instance of damage by 100% and Stagnate nearby targets, then cast Resonance Skill Pinpoint Strike, dealing Spectro DMG and additionally reducing their Vibration Strength by 5%. The DMG taken by Zani is reduced by 30% within the next 2s.

Crisis Response Protocol

When Zani is not in Inferno Mode and has full Redundant Energy, her Resonance Skill is replaced with Resonance Skill Crisis Response Protocol.

Hold Resonance Skill to enter Ready Stance. While in Ready Stance, Zani is immune to interruption. This state ends early if Zani is switched off the field. After releasing Resonance Skill button or when the stance duration ends, consume all Redundant Energy to cast Targeted Action, dealing Spectro DMG.

When attacked by the enemy in Ready Stance, reduce this instance of damage by 100% and consume all Redundant Energy to cast Forcible Riposte, dealing Spectro DMG, Stagnating the target, and further reducing their Vibration Strength by 5%. The DMG taken by Zani is reduced by 30% within the next 2s.

Casting Targeted Action or Forcible Riposte inflicts a stack of Heliacal Ember upon the target on hit and recovers Blaze before entering Sunburst mode.

Sunburst

The Spectro Frazzle DMG dealt by Zani to the target is Amplified by 20%.

skills.name: Between Dawn and Dusk
skills.description:
Rekindle

Deal Spectro DMG and enter Inferno Mode, increasing Max Blaze from 100 to 150 and granting 50 Blazes. When in Inferno Mode, the DMG Multiplier of Basic Attack is increased.

The Last Stand

When in Inferno Mode, Resonance Liberation The Last Stand becomes available when Blaze is lower than 30 or after 8s in Inferno Mode.

Casting Resonance Liberation The Last Stand deals Spectro DMG and ends the Inferno Mode.

skills.name: There Will Be A Light
skills.description:
Heliacal Ember

When Zani is in the team and a nearby Resonator inflicts Spectro Frazzle upon a target, immediately consume all Spectro Frazzle stacks and trigger the corresponding DMG, then convert Spectro Frazzle into an equal number of Heliacal Embers. Every time the conversion happens, Zani obtains Blaze based on the stacks of Heliacal Ember inflicted. Heliacal Ember is capped at 60 stacks, with each stack lasting for 6s. Heliacal Ember stacks are counted toward the Spectro Frazzle stacks for the Eternal Radiance Sonata Effect.

Scorching Light

When Zani is in Inferno Mode, Heavy Slash - Daybreak, Heavy Slash - Dawning, Heavy Slash - Nightfall, and Heavy Slash - Lightsmash become available, which deal Spectro DMG that is considered both Heavy Attack DMG and Spectro Frazzle DMG.

  • When Blaze is higher than 30, Resonance Skill Standard Defense Protocol is replaced with Resonance Skill Scorching Light.

  • Hold Resonance Skill to enter Ready Stance, during which Zani is immune to interruption. This state ends early when Zani is switched off the field. Release Resonance Skill button to consume Blaze and perform Heavy Slash - Daybreak.

  • When attacked in a certain time after entering Ready Stance, reduce this instance of damage by 100% and Stagnate nearby targets, then perform Heavy Slash - Lightsmash, consuming Blazes and further reducing their Vibration Strength by 10%. The DMG taken within the next 2s is reduced by 30%.

  • After casting Heavy Slash - Lightsmash, Basic Attack is replaced with Heavy Slash - Nightfall, consuming up to 40 Blazes on hit, with each Blaze increasing the DMG Multiplier of Heavy Slash - Nightfall.

  • When Ready Stance ends, immediately perform Heavy Slash - Nightfall.

  • When Blaze is higher than 30, Basic Attack is replaced with Heavy Slash - Daybreak. After entering Inferno Mode, casting Basic Attack immediately replaces the current Basic Attack with Resonance Skill Scorching Light. Hold Basic Attack to enter Ready Stance.

  • After performing Heavy Slash - Daybreak, Basic Attack is replaced with Heavy Slash - Dawning when Zani has more than 30 Blazes. Heavy Slash - Dawning consumes Blazes. After performing Heavy Slash - Dawning, Basic Attack is replaced with Heavy Slash - Nightfall.

  • If Basic Attack is not replaced with Heavy Slash - Nightfall after a successful Dodge, press Normal Attack within a certain time to perform Heavy Slash - Lightsmash at the cost of Blazes.

Redundant Energy

Zani can hold up to 100 Redundant Energy.

  • Obtain Redundant Energy when Normal Attacks hit a target.

  • Obtain Redundant Energy when Intro Skill Immediate Execution hits a target.

  • Obtain Redundant Energy when casting Resonance Skill Standard Defense Protocol.

  • Obtain Redundant Energy when casting Pinpoint Strike.

  • Cannot obtain Redundant Energy while in Inferno Mode.

Blaze

Blaze is capped at 100 when not in Inferno Mode.

  • Blaze is capped at 150 in Inferno Mode.

  • Casting Targeted Action or Forcible Riposte grants 10 Blazes.

  • Every stack of Heliacal Ember converted from Spectro Frazzle grants 5 Blazes.

  • Casting Resonance Liberation Rekindle grants 50 Blazes.

profile.calculationsNotes:
Important!

  • Sequence 2: If you're not already using a CRIT DMG main echo on Zani after unlocking this sequence it gains even more value in most team and weapon set-ups.
  • Sequence 6: Outside of raw damage increases this sequence also grants Zani additional Blaze which allows her to perform 3 sequences of Forte empowered basics instead of her usual 2. We recommend altering your play and rotation accordingly.

Rotation time after Sequences: Post S6: 16.34s.

weapons.Comment: Zani's Signature weapon is by far her best option, thanks to its massive boosts in her best stats: 48.6% CRIT DMG with high ATK, 50% Spectro Frazzle Amplification, and even 8% DEF Ignore with a simple condition (that can be permanently triggered during any part of Zani's rotation). How much stronger this weapon is compared to other options depends on how many other sources of Frazzle Amplify you have access to. For example, with Phoebe's 100% Frazzle Amplify applied, the value of this weapon is diminished due to dilution, but without it, it becomes far more important.

Roccia's weapon is an amazing choice on Zani as all her attacks during her Ultimate stance are the Heavy Attack type while still being treated as Basic Attack casts for the purpose of this weapon's passive, giving her 48% Heavy DMG Bonus combined with an extra 24.3% CRIT Rate and high ATK make it the second best choice.

Beyond the usual high Base ATK, CRIT Rate and all-type DMG bonus buffs Xiangli Yao's weapon provides, Zani makes little use of the extra Liberation DMG Bonus effect so this weapon is comparably weaker than other options, but can still be considered as a good alternative due to raw stats alone.
The best permanently available option for Zani which acts as a nice ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for her.

Simple ATK, CRIT Rate and Liberation DMG stat-stick for Zani who does not benefit from this weapon's DEF Ignore-related effects. Suffers from a low Base ATK and too much CRIT Rate causing Zani to easily overcap.

The extra Energy Regen and huge ATK boosts this weapon provides are very useful to Zani, but she has little use for the rest of its passive boosting Basic and Skill DMG. With that said, it remains the best permanently available choice thanks to its really high Base ATK and small Energy Regen boost.

This Battle Pass exclusive is focused on buffing Liberation DMG which Zani barely benefits from, but luckily for her the CRIT DMG and ATK stats provided by this weapon are used well on her which makes it the best 4-star choice for her.

One of the best 4-star weapons on Zani thanks to its solid Base ATK, ATK-increasing effects, and ability to restore flat Energy when Resonance Skill is cast, which eases Zani's build requirements requiring no Energy Regen at all.

Similarly to Aether Strike, this Battle Pass exclusive is focused on buffing Liberation DMG which Zani barely benefits from, but Zani does benefit from the CRIT Rate stat this weapon has. Not better than the above 4-stars because it only buffs Liberation DMG and not ATK which Zani would prefer.

Provides some extra ATK increase over Legend of Drunken Hero which is dependent on not getting hit to upkeep. Even in the best conditions for this weapon, it's only slightly higher than the craftable, making it not recommended if better options are available.

While this Rinascita craftable looks like it'd work well on Zani as she is a Negative Status character, unfortunately for her Heliacal Ember (which she converts Spectro Frazzle into) does not count as a Negative Status, which makes its passive only benefit Zani if Ciaccona or Chisa are on the team to apply other Negative Statuses than Spectro Frazzle. Seeing as neither are top teammate choices for her, this weapon is only used as a last resort F2P option.

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Spectro DMG% boost, a 20% CRIT RATE buff for 15 seconds after inflicting Spectro Frazzle and further 15% Spectro DMG% boost for 15 seconds after attacking an enemy that has 10 Spectro Frazzle Stacks. For characters that have the capability to inflict Spectro Frazzle in their kit the 20% CRIT RATE boost is close to permanent, while the 15% Spectro DMG boost should maintain decent uptime in Spectro Frazzle focused teams. Generally the best in slot set for all DPS characters capable of inflicting Spectro Frazzle.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Offers an unconditional 12% Spectro DMG and 12% Heavy Attack DMG boost when active in a resonator's Main Echo Slot, making it a solid choice for Spectro focused resonators who emphasize Heavy Attack damage and are looking to use the 5P Eternal Radiance set bonus.
echoes.Echo_2_Comment: Offers an unconditional 12% Spectro DMG boost when active in a resonators Main Echo Slot and gains a 100% DMG bonus to its attack against enemies inflicted by Spectro Frazzle. This echo is the go-to choice for most resonators capable of inflicting Spectro Frazzle, who are focusing on damage and are looking to use the 5P Eternal Radiance set bonus.

synergies.Comment: Phoebe in her Confession mode is the perfect Zani teammate. Providing 100% DMG Amplification, able to run a supportive set like Moonlit Clouds for extra damage and also being able to fully fill Zani's Blaze bar by applying lots of Spectro Frazzle, no teammate choice Zani has can compare to Phoebe, making her the best Zani team choice by huge amounts.

These two are the other Spectro Frazzle appliers Zani has to try to fill her Blaze bar. While neither compare to Phoebe, having 2 Frazzle appliers in the team they can allow Zani to execute 3 Nightfalls per rotation (with some quickswap if Phoebe + Spectro Rover is used) for extra damage, making Phoebe + Spectro Rover the best Zani team when fully optimized (with Ciaccona as a worse alternative if need be).

All 3 of these characters can Amplify Zani's Heavy Attack DMG via their Outros to buff her damage further. While none of them quite compete with Phoebe's 100% Amplification, Phrolova has a lot of personal damage to her name and Mortefi is F2P-accessible with higher buffing. Iuno is an in-between of the two with extra sustain.

As the best generalist Support, it's no surprise Shorekeeper can slot in any team in the game as she provides high team-wide ATK%, 15% DMG Amplification, CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG buffs making her the best option for Zani teams without quickswap (she also has much higher sustain than Spectro Rover if that's desired!)
